Coastal Land Conversion Project

Portions of the analytical workflow development and code refinement were assisted by an AI-based large language model (ChatGPT, OpenAI). The tool was used to support statistical model comparison strategies, cross-validation implementation, and reproducible R code structuring. All data processing, model execution, interpretation of results, and scientific conclusions were performed and verified by the authors. The authors take full responsibility for the integrity, accuracy, and interpretation of the analyses presented.

Rationale: to look at more localized drivers of VRR based on Molino et al., 2023 hypothesis that these are dependent on local drivers. https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1029/2023JG007525

Datasets:

1) vertical retreat rate

Dataset from: Chen and Kirwan 2023 https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/gcb.17081 
- vertical forest retreat rates for every point along the mid-Atlantic https://portal.edirepository.org/nis/mapbrowse?packageid=knb-lter-vcr.399.1


2) threshold elevations

Dataset from: Molino et al 2022 https://aslopubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/lol2.10262 
- threshold elevation defining the boundary between forest and marsh, aggregated by watershed. This is only for Maryland and Virginia, so won’t work for EXCHANGE sites in DE or NJ
https://portal.edirepository.org/nis/mapbrowse?packageid=knb-lter-vcr.343.2

3) Watershed parameters from Molino et al 2022 

4) Soil parameters from EC1 v3 

https://data.ess-dive.lbl.gov/view/doi%3A10.15485%2F1960313


Analysis to be completed in this script:

1) Multiple linear regression of vertical retreat rate vs. EC1 soil parameters 

2) Multiple linear regression of threshold elevations vs. EC1 soil parameters (+ identified watershed parameters from Molino et al)

For WRT:
α is a scale parameter that is inversely proportional to the mean pore diameter; n is a shape parameter that controls the slope of the soil-water characteristic curve; θr is the residual water content, and θs is the saturated water content.

### Clean and merge datasets 

#### EXCHANGE datasets and metadata

```{r cleaning data, warnings=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
ec1_meta_curated <- ec1_meta %>%
  full_join(ec1_meta_kit, by="kit_id") %>%
  filter(region == "Mid-Atlantic") %>%
  #can't do this analysis on the wetland, sediment or water data
  #Want to look for the variables for the upland, though
  filter(transect_location %in% c("upland")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(latitude)) %>%
  dplyr::select(kit_id, region, transect_location, site_name, latitude, longitude, elevation_m, soil_type, soil_horizon)

ec1_meta_curated

ec1_soil_all <- ec1_bd %>%
  full_join(ec1_cond, by=c("campaign", "kit_id", "transect_location")) %>%
  full_join(ec1_gwc, by=c("campaign", "kit_id", "transect_location")) %>%
  full_join(ec1_ph, by=c("campaign", "kit_id", "transect_location")) %>%
  full_join(ec1_mineralogy, by=c("campaign", "kit_id", "transect_location")) %>%
  full_join(ec1_texture, by=c("campaign", "kit_id", "transect_location")) %>%
  full_join(ec1_wrc, by=c("campaign", "kit_id", "transect_location")) %>%
  inner_join(ec1_meta_curated, by=c("kit_id","transect_location"))

ec1_soil_all
```


#### Vertical Forest Retreat Rate

Projected Coordinate Reference System (CRS) "WGS 84 / UTM zone 18N" = EPSG code for this CRS is 32618.

```{r data extracting, echo=FALSE}

# Focusing on upland sites for lat and long: 
coordinates <- ec1_meta_curated %>%
  dplyr::select(kit_id, transect_location, longitude, latitude) %>% 
   filter(!(kit_id == "K055" & transect_location == "upland"),
          !(kit_id == "K058" & transect_location == "upland"),
          !(kit_id == "K042" & transect_location == "upland"),
         !(kit_id == "K042" & transect_location == "transition"),
          !(kit_id == "K045" & transect_location == "upland"),
         !(kit_id == "K045" & transect_location == "transition"),
          !(kit_id == "K048" & transect_location == "upland"),
         !(kit_id == "K048" & transect_location == "transition")
  ) # no retreat data here

coordinates_sf <- st_as_sf(coordinates, coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326)

# Transform the CRS to match the shapefile
coordinates_sf_transformed <- st_transform(coordinates_sf, 32618)

extracted_vfrr_data <- st_join(coordinates_sf_transformed, vfrr_shp, join = st_intersects)

extracted_vfrr_no_geometry <- st_set_geometry(extracted_vfrr_data, NULL)

extracted_vfrr_df <- as.data.frame(extracted_vfrr_no_geometry) %>%
  #filter out the -9999 values
  filter(V_RetreatR > 0 & V_RetreatR < 99) %>%
  #filter out places with NAs
  filter(!is.na(V_RetreatR))

```

### dataframe with all EC1 data, Molino data for Vertical Retreat Rate:

```{r data merging, echo=FALSE}
clc_all_data <- extracted_vfrr_df %>%
  inner_join(ec1_soil_all, by= c("kit_id","transect_location")) %>%
  left_join(ec1_water_sal, by = "kit_id")

clc_all_data
```

#### Threshold Elevations 

Projected CRS: NAD83 / UTM zone 18N = crs epsg 26918 aka should be the same as  st_crs(HUC_shp)
```{r data extracting in other crs, echo=FALSE}

ec1_meta_curated_2 <- ec1_meta %>%
  full_join(ec1_meta_kit, by="kit_id") %>%
  filter(region == "Mid-Atlantic") %>%
  #can't do this analysis on the wetland, sediment or water data
  filter(transect_location %in% c("upland")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(latitude)) %>%
  dplyr::select(kit_id, region, transect_location, site_name, latitude, longitude, elevation_m, soil_type, soil_horizon)

coordinates_ws <- ec1_meta_curated_2 %>%
  dplyr::select(kit_id, transect_location, longitude, latitude) 

coordinates_sf_1 <- st_as_sf(coordinates_ws, coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326)

# Transform the CRS to match the shapefile
coordinates_ws_sf_transformed <- st_transform(coordinates_sf_1, 26918)


points_in_watershed <- st_join(coordinates_ws_sf_transformed, HUC_shp, join = st_within) %>%
  drop_na()



```

### dataframe with all EC1 data for Threshold Elevation:

```{r data merging elevation, echo=FALSE}
clc_all_data_ws
```

# Refit original model with just macro variables on just the 17 sites that overlap with EXCHANGE data. 

From Molino et al https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1029/2023JG007525
Variable	p-value	Coefficient	Resolution	Source
Tidal range	0.001	0.2264	400 m	NOAA%20%20VDatum
Surface salinity	0.000	0.0083	600 m	St-Laurent et al. (2020)
Average slope	0.003	0.1304	30 m	Molino et al. (2020)
```{r subset}
d17 <- clc_all_data_ws_sigcors %>% 
  group_by(name) %>%
  dplyr::select(Elevation,
         Surface_Salinity,
         Tidal_Range,
         Average_Slope,
         surface_water_sal_psu,
         moisturecontent_perc_drywtbasis,
         bulk_density_g_cm3,
         specific_conductance_us_cm) %>%
  drop_na() %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(-name)

d17
```
```{r macro variables on subset}
cor(d17[, c("Elevation","Tidal_Range","Surface_Salinity","Average_Slope")])

```
Macro variables are highly co-correlated in the subset data, so pick the one with the highest correlation to elevation. This is actually slope, not salinity 

```{r correlation matrix local variables}
corr_matrix <- cor(d17, method = "pearson") # Uses pairs only when we have complete observations 
    
# Print the correlation matrix using corrplot
library(corrplot) # Needed for the correlation plot
corrplot(corr_matrix, method = "color", type = "lower", tl.col = "black", tl.srt = 45, title = sprintf("Correlation Matrix (Threshold: %s)", corr_threshold = 0.5))

labels <- c(
 # Surface_Salinity = "Watershed Average Salinity (PSU)",
  #Tidal_Range = "Tidal Range",
 # Average_Slope = "Average Slope",
  surface_water_sal_psu = "Adjacent Surface Water Salinity (PSU)",
  moisturecontent_perc_drywtbasis = "Soil Moisture Content (% dry wt basis)",
  bulk_density_g_cm3 = "Soil Bulk Density (g/cm³)",
  specific_conductance_us_cm = "Soil Specific Conductance (µS/cm)"
)

corr_df <- data.frame(corr_matrix["Elevation", -1]) %>%
  rename(Correlation_w_Elevation = 'corr_matrix..Elevation....1.') %>%
  rownames_to_column(var = "Variable") %>%
  filter(Variable != c("Surface_Salinity", "Tidal_Range", "Average_Slope"))

plot_corr <- ggplot(corr_df,
       aes(x = reorder(Variable, Correlation_w_Elevation),
           y = Correlation_w_Elevation,
           fill= Variable)) +
  geom_col(alpha=0.7) +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_classic() +
  ylab("Pearson Correlation with Threshold Elevation") +
  xlab("EC1 Measured Variable") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = labels)+
  scale_fill_manual(values = soilpalettes::soil_palette("redox2", 9)) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

corr_df

plot_corr
ggsave("corr_matrix_forproposal.png", plot = plot_corr)
    
```

```{r n16}
m_macro_ws <- lm(Elevation ~ Average_Slope, data = d17)
summary(m_macro_ws)

loocv_rmse(Elevation ~ Average_Slope, d17)

summary(m_micro_ws)

m_combo_ws <- lm(Elevation ~ Average_Slope +
                               surface_water_sal_psu +
                               moisturecontent_perc_drywtbasis,
                 data = d17)

summary(m_combo_ws)

loocv_rmse(Elevation ~ surface_water_sal_psu +
                           moisturecontent_perc_drywtbasis, d17)

loocv_rmse(Elevation ~ Average_Slope +
                           surface_water_sal_psu +
                           moisturecontent_perc_drywtbasis, d17)

```

```{r n13}
d13 <- clc_all_data_ws_sigcors %>%
  dplyr::select(Elevation,
         Average_Slope,
         th_s,
         alpha) %>%
  drop_na()

m_macro13 <- lm(Elevation ~ Average_Slope, data = d13)
m_micro13 <- lm(Elevation ~ th_s + alpha, data = d13)
m_combo13 <- lm(Elevation ~ Average_Slope + th_s + alpha, data = d13)

summary(m_macro13)
summary(m_micro13)
summary(m_combo13)

loocv_rmse(Elevation ~ Average_Slope, d13)
loocv_rmse(Elevation ~ th_s + alpha, d13)
loocv_rmse(Elevation ~ Average_Slope + th_s + alpha, d13)

```
tl;dr is that the local site characteristics aggregated at the watershed scale/using watershed scale threshold elevations doesn't add in significant explanatory power over the watershed scale variables. so, lets find and aggregate some watershed scale soil properties!

# Part 2: Database data 

```{r set up to extract data}
library(sf)
library(soilDB)
library(terra)

HUC_shp_ea <- st_transform(HUC_shp, 5070)

# 1) Request mukey grid again (start a bit coarser if needed)
mukey_r <- mukey.wcs(aoi = HUC_shp_ea, db = "gSSURGO", res = 150)

# 2) Convert -> write to disk -> read back (forces values to exist)
tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".tif")
writeRaster(rast(mukey_r), tmp, overwrite = TRUE)

mukey_rast <- rast(tmp)

# 3) Confirm it now has values
hasValues(mukey_rast)
global(mukey_rast, "notNA", na.rm = TRUE)
```


bulk density (dbthirdbar_r)
clay (claytotal_r)
sand (sandtotal_r)
available water capacity (awc_r)

```{r pull data}
vars <- c("dbthirdbar_r", "claytotal_r", "sandtotal_r", "awc_r")

# Example: fetch property table for mukeys you have in your grid
# (you’ll need to extract unique mukeys from the mukey raster first)
mukeys <- sort(unique(values(mukey_rast)))
mukeys <- mukeys[!is.na(mukeys)]

prop <- get_SDA_property(
  mukeys = mukeys,
  property = vars,
  top_depth = 0,
  bottom_depth = 30,
  method = "Dominant Component",
  agg.method = "Depth Weighted Average"
)
```
